hook_text: 3,457 m or 3,5 m — which jump wins? The one with more digits loses.
clip_script: Compare the jumps: 3,457, 3,5 and 3,45. Write them with three decimal places: 3,457, 3,500 and 3,450. Units: all three. Tenths: four, five and four. So 3,500 is the largest. The classic error is to think that a decimal with more digits is larger, because that rule works for whole numbers. 3,457 has more digits than 3,5 but is smaller.
visual_style: Three long-jump landing marks in a sand pit with measuring tapes; zeros slide in to line up the digits; the tenths digits light up and 3,5 wins.
pacing: Quick jumps, pause on the trap, line-up animation, winner reveal.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson to round any decimal like a scoreboard.
